ideas: Where you'll live and what work you'll do
What you'll need to do to get there

phrases.meaning: healthy mix of job and free time
do your job away from the office
a home that belongs to me
think about something in the past

model: By 2035 I'll be in my late thirties, so I've actually thought about this quite a lot. First of all, I hope I'll have a place of my own, maybe a small house on the edge of Da Nang with a garden. Although I love the energy of big cities, I don't want to raise children in heavy traffic and pollution. In terms of work, I'd like to be leading a small team of software designers. I'm not obsessed with climbing the career ladder, but I'd like to be respected in my field. Ideally, I'll be able to work remotely at least a few days a week, because a good work-life balance matters more to me than a big title. I also hope I'll have settled down by then, with a partner and maybe one or two kids. Being financially independent is important too. While it's true that house prices are rising fast, I've already started saving, and a small amount is transferred into an investment account every month. Last year I was offered a job in Singapore with a much higher salary, and although I was tempted, I turned it down because it didn't fit this long-term picture. Of course, I know that sometimes things don't go to plan, and a lot can change in ten years. But I'd like to look back on this decade and feel that my big decisions were made for the right reasons.
